albums.blurb: Santaolalla is the Argentine producer and composer who went on to win back-to-back Oscars for the Brokeback Mountain and Babel scores; in the 1990s he was best known for producing Latin rock records, including Café Tacvba's Re. Ronroco, released on Nonesuch in 1998, was his turn from the mixing desk to his own music: twelve quiet solo pieces on the ronroco, a deeper-voiced cousin of the Andean charango, with Aníbal Kerpel adding touches of vibraphone and melodica. There are no vocals anywhere on the record.
albums.reception: Michael Mann licensed its track "Iguazu" for The Insider in 1999 after hearing the album, which effectively launched Santaolalla's film-scoring career, and Nonesuch gave the record its first vinyl issue as a remaster in 2024.

albums.blurb: Ruban Nielson's Portland-based project released II on Jagjaguwar in February 2013, between the scuzzy self-titled debut and the funkier Multi-Love. Recorded and produced by Nielson himself, it keeps the warped, home-taped guitar sound but opens it out into road-weary songwriting — "So Good at Being in Trouble" and "Swim and Sleep (Like a Shark)" are its center of gravity. The Spotify link is the deluxe edition, which carries the full original album plus a handful of extras.
albums.reception: II holds a 78/100 on Metacritic, indicating generally favorable reviews, with Pitchfork scoring it 7.3 and critics widely noting it as a lonelier, more refined record than the band's debut.

albums.blurb: Caldwell was a Miami singer-songwriter whose self-titled 1978 debut came out on Clouds, an imprint of the disco powerhouse TK Records. The label famously kept his face off the cover — a silhouette on a park bench — so R&B radio and audiences wouldn't know he was white, and the record's smooth, jazz-chorded soul made him a lasting favorite with that audience. Later reissues retitled the album What You Won't Do for Love after its hit, which is how Spotify lists it; it has since become a yacht-rock touchstone and a staple sample source, most famously in 2Pac's "Do for Love".
albums.reception: The album reached No. 21 on the Billboard 200, while the title single hit No. 9 on the Hot 100 and No. 6 on the R&B chart.
